etymologies.etymologyHTML: From French nationalisme. By surface analysis, national +‎ -ism.

definitions.definition: Patriotism; the idea of supporting one's country, people or culture.

quote.citation: 1927 May, Quincy Wright, “Bolshevist Influences in China”, in Current History‎[1], volume XXVI, number 2, →ISSN, →OCLC, page 300, column 1:
quote.text: Perhaps the explanation of the Chinese situation most generally accepted by historians is nationalism, a phenomenon which has always occurred when a people of distinctive cultural characteristics becomes aware of foreign domination. Napoleonic domination in Italy and Germany a century ago created nationalism there, as did Turkish domination in the Balkans and the Arab countries.

quote.citation: 2017, Meir Litvak, Constructing Nationalism in Iran:
quote.text: Following the 1979 Revolution, Khomeini came out against nationalism.

definitions.definition: Support for the creation of a sovereign nation (which does not currently exist).
(UK, Ireland) Support for the union of Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland.
